questions.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

In addition, we've been given that

$$
∇f(x,y)=\operatorname{arctan}⁡y\,i+\frac{x}{1+{y}^{2}}\,j.
$$

First, we substitute $x={t}^{2}+1$ and $y=t$ into $∇f(x,y)$ to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡t\,i+\frac{{t}^{2}+1}{1+{t}^{2}}\,j \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡t\,i+j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j \\  & =2t\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\operatorname{arctan}⁡t\,i+j)\cdot (2t\,i+j) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡t\cdot 2t+1\cdot 1 \\  & =2t\operatorname{arctan}⁡t+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the above at $t=1,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(1))] & =2(1)\operatorname{arctan}⁡1+1 \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}+1 \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}+1 \\  & =\frac{\pi +2}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Compute the rate of change of the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2},2t-1⟩$ at the point $t=0.$
questions.worked_solution:
The rate of change of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)$ is given by $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$ To calculate this, we can use the chain rule.

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}),\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2x,-2y⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={t}^{2}$ and $y=2t-1$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =⟨2{t}^{2},-2(2t-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{t}^{2},2-4t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨2{t}^{2},2-4t⟩\cdot ⟨2t,2⟩ \\  & =2{t}^{2}\cdot 2t+(2-4t)\cdot 2 \\  & =4{t}^{3}-8t+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $f$ along the curve $r(t)$ at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(0))] & =4(0)^{3}-8(0)+4 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Compute the rate of change of the function $f(x,y,z)=xyz$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)=⟨2t,\sqrt{t},3t-1⟩$ at the point $t=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The rate of change of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)$ is given by $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$ To calculate this, we can use the chain rule.

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(xyz),\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz),\frac{∂}{∂z}(xyz)⟩ \\  & =⟨yz,xz,xy⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=2t,y=\sqrt{t}$ and $z=3t-1$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =⟨\sqrt{t}(3t-1),2t(3t-1),2t\sqrt{t}⟩ \\  & =⟨(3t-1)\sqrt{t},6{t}^{2}-2t,2t\sqrt{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨(3t-1)\sqrt{t},6{t}^{2}-2t,2t\sqrt{t}⟩\cdot ⟨2,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},3⟩ \\  & =(3t-1)\sqrt{t}\cdot 2+(6{t}^{2}-2t)\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}+2t\sqrt{t}\cdot 3 \\  & =6t\sqrt{t}-2\sqrt{t}+\frac{3{t}^{2}-t}{\sqrt{t}}+6t\sqrt{t} \\  & =12t\sqrt{t}-2\sqrt{t}+\frac{3{t}^{2}-t}{\sqrt{t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $f$ along the curve $r(t)$ at $t=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(1))] & =12(1)\sqrt{1}-2\sqrt{1}+\frac{3(1)^{2}-1}{\sqrt{1}} \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =-{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡{t}^{2}\,i+{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡{t}^{2}\,j+{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡{t}^{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,k \\  & =2t\,i+{e}^{t}\,j+{e}^{t}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(-{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡{t}^{2}\,i+{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡{t}^{2}\,j+{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡{t}^{2}\,k)\cdot (2t\,i+{e}^{t}\,j+{e}^{t}\,k) \\  & =-2t{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡{t}^{2}+{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡{t}^{2}\cdot {e}^{t}+{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡{t}^{2}\cdot {e}^{t} \\  & =-2t{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡{t}^{2}+2{e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡{t}^{2} \\  & =2{e}^{2t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡{t}^{2}-t\operatorname{sin}⁡{t}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,j+2{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})\,k \\  & =\,i+2\,j-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,j+2{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,k)\cdot (\,i+2\,j-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,k) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\cdot 1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\cdot 2+2{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\cdot (-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t).\end{aligned}
$$
